name: Diplomacy (Wargame)
description: Classic negotiation and strategy board game of pre-WWI European great power politics designed by Allan Calhamer. Seven players represent the major powers; there are no dice—outcomes depend entirely on negotiation, alliance formation, and betrayal. Online multiplayer versions (webDiplomacy, Backstabbr) enable asynchronous play. Models complex inter-state alliance dynamics that produce emergent and often chaotic diplomatic outcomes unpredictable from initial positions.
reputation: classic in international relations education; used at Harvard Kennedy School and other policy programs; strong AI research interest (Meta's Cicero AI agent trained on Diplomacy)
notes: Published by Avalon Hill 1959; current edition by Hasbro. Widely studied in AI research: Meta's Cicero (2022) achieved human-level performance combining language models with strategic reasoning. Online platforms include webDiplomacy.net and Backstabbr. Zero luck mechanics make it a pure test of negotiation and strategy. Note: a separate benchmark card (diplomacy.json) covers the DipNet AI benchmark based on this game.
